title: Raise conditional κ to 0.00389011528360 using weighted source complements
body:
## Result

**Conditional κ ≥ 0.00389011528360** at the fixed carrier of [#8029](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8029). The complete improvement is exactly `0.00000000001219` over its `0.00389011527141`. The signed test is `0.00389011528367` with ordinary BIT cap `0.003890115283681`.

The actual 768-factor source and exit laws permit a higher separated trial (`0.003890115286593`) and a smaller terminal debit (`869/H` instead of `1524/H`, with `H=299610000000000`). The proof uses a complete paid-rank moment and a bound on the capacity of each root or deeper source group. It charges all eligible split remainders and covers every rank by 320 finite cells plus an infinite-height bound. The carrier, admissible cover prime, 36 BIT calls, 48 rational calls and signed application use the same physical construction. The raw BIT upper remains `0.003890115286595`, which is `0.000000000002995` above the new lower. The new lower exceeds even that upper minus #8029's `1524/H` debit by `4177787/1997400000000000000`.

## Sources and overlap

The separate CI prerequisite `0618e75a22cec54d1651394ef83d088551b7f026` is the exact [#7257](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7257) repair reused by #8029 for the CI guide and historical snapshot.

The package authenticates the exact 50-file predecessor tree, 30-file paired package and 134-file application closure offline.
- [#8026](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8026) at `d9c3e9ad79686d863cb30cf00f1e32e6c7461300` established source grouping, a height-dependent root-share bound and one-small-remainder accounting on the 451-factor supplier. The paired-word extension uses two change-of-measure windows to fund the actual cutoff groups and direct completed paid moments to control the exits at all heights. [Prior small-remainder proof](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d9c3e9ad79686d863cb30cf00f1e32e6c7461300/research/bit-451-height-dependent-sources/small-remainders/PROOF.md)

This work keeps the #8029 carrier. The [P104 discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19799234) records related changed-word screens.

## Validation and premises

The clean #8029 verifier reproduced `0.00389011527141` in 798 s. The complete successor replay passed in 199 s on CPython 3.12 with 54 strict and four functional checks. The registered command below independently completed on the same package bytes in 205 s. Two pricing engines check the separated trial. The signed replay recounts both invoices, rebuilds the native and converted operators, checks ownership, restoration and precision fixtures, and covers the four ordinary stock stages and outer application. Controls reject one fewer terminal debit unit, the old uniform source bound for this logarithmic power, an extra paid rank-one call on either side, a BIT cap equal to the tested point and a cap below the effective requirement.

```sh
python3.12 -IB scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-paired-source-complements
```

The five inherited premises cover native action on every column, owned storage and erasure, compiler transfer, precision and tape services, and analytic recovery. The production-scale stock is certified from its fixed source and checked premises. The proof and deterministic receipt are in the package.

## Credit and next question

Ali Romman supplied the paired circuits and complete application, ToikY the fixed-carrier paid-moment predecessor, Jacob Alan Sussman the integer flow, DreamingOfClouds the ambient-cap and delayed-cover proofs, and zxv the weighted-exit and shifted-log bounds. OpenAI Codex materially assisted the new proof, software and verification.

Can a changed literal BIT rank clear the current raw upper with all operator and restoration checks? The first test is a changed signed invoice with a directed positive margin in both price engines.
